Good — I've got what I need. Here's my assessment of the two changelogs against what `email-automation/` actually does.

## Bottom line

One update is genuinely worth acting on (**Personal Access Tokens**); the rest are either not relevant to a solo CLI or "note it, no action yet."

## Worth acting on

**Personal Access Tokens (Beta) — app release v7.1, July 7 2026**
> "Create and manage scoped API tokens directly in the app"

This is the one that maps directly onto pain in this repo. Right now `src/cakemail-client.ts` does the full OAuth refresh-token dance: exchange `CAKEMAIL_REFRESH_TOKEN` → short-lived access token on every run, detect a rotated refresh token, write it back into the root `.env` mid-run, and fall back to `npm run refresh-cakemail` (username+password, `grant_type=password`) when it fully expires. That write-back-to-`.env` rotation is fragile and is exactly the kind of thing a static, scoped token removes.

A PAT would let you:
- Drop the refresh-token rotation + `.env` write-back logic and the `refresh-cakemail.ts` recovery path.
- Store one long-lived `CAKEMAIL_ACCESS_TOKEN` (scoped to what this CLI needs: transactional send, campaigns, contacts/lists, reports).
- Reduce the blast radius vs. a token that can mint full-account access.

Caveats before you touch it: it's **Beta**, and the web search couldn't find it in the public API docs yet — so confirm the token works with `POST /token`-less Bearer auth (i.e. used directly as `Authorization: Bearer <PAT>`) against your account before ripping out the refresh flow. This is a ~1–2 hr change and set-and-forget after. I'd treat it as a "do it next time you're in `cakemail-client.ts`" rather than urgent, since auto-rotation currently works (per your memory note).

## Note it, but no action warranted now

- **Tag filtering improvements (API v1.18, Jun 25 2026)** — Potentially relevant to the refresher-audience workflow, which today cross-references CSV migration exports by hand (`migration/*.csv`) and a brittle date table. *If* the API now supports server-side tag include/exclude queries, you could build the "Interested − DO-NOT-NOTIFY − already-attended" audience via API instead of CSV. But the changelog is one vague line with no endpoint detail, and per your action-litmus this isn't worth chasing until you're actually running the next refresher.
- **Webhooks: `User.Confirmed` / `User.Deleted` / `User.Created` (v1.18)** — You have Netlify functions that *could* consume these (e.g. react to DOI confirmations/unsubscribes), but there's no current use case that polling doesn't already cover. Skip until a concrete need appears.
- **Engagement segmentation (v7.1)** — "Dynamic segments from how contacts interact." Overlaps conceptually with the `aiquiz` nurture, but it's a UI feature, not something the CLI drives. No action.
- **Email API thumbnail rendering / rendering fixes (v1.18)** — Not relevant to your transactional/campaign sends.

## One correction for CLAUDE.md eventually

Your `email-automation/CLAUDE.md` says *"No official maintained Node.js SDK."* Still true for **Node** — but Cakemail now publishes an official [`cakemail/cakemail-php`](https://github.com/cakemail/cakemail-php) SDK plus (per their dev portal) a CLI and MCP server. Doesn't change your raw-`fetch` approach, but the "no SDK at all" framing is now slightly stale — the accurate statement is "no official *Node* SDK."

Want me to prototype the PAT swap in `cakemail-client.ts` behind a feature check (fall back to the refresh flow if the PAT env var isn't set), so you can test it without committing to the cutover?

Sources:
- [Cakemail release notes (v7.1, v7.0)](https://www.cakemail.com/releases)
- [Next-gen API changelog v1.18](https://docs.cakemail.com/en/resources-support/changelog/next-gen-api-v118)
- [Cakemail API auth / token docs](https://cakemail.dev/en/api/token)
- [cakemail/cakemail-php SDK](https://github.com/cakemail/cakemail-php)
